We need to apply template 1679747 to the molecule (initial_molecule SMILES: C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2). The template is given in mapped_rxn: 'O=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1.[Li][CH2:1][Si](C)(C)C>>[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][c:6]([O:7][CH3:8])[cH:9][cH:10]1)[c:11]1[cH:12][cH:13][c:14]([O:15][CH3:16])[cH:17][cH:18]1'

So forward reaction: a carbonyl (O= C) attached to aromatic rings plus LiCH2Si(C)(C)C (a silyl carbanion) gives product: CH2= C( aromatic ) aromatic (i.e., a stilbene with methoxy groups). The template is a Wittig-type? Actually it's a Wittig reaction: aldehyde + phosphonium ylide? But here LiCH2Si(C)(C)C is a carbanion (maybe a silyl carbanion). Anyway.

Our target molecule is C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2 which is a trans-stilbene with two anisole rings (para-methoxy). The template likely breaks the C=C double bond to give an aldehyde (or ketone) and a silyl carbanion.

Applying retrosynthetic template to target should give precursors: the aldehyde (or ketone) O= C( aromatic ) aromatic? Actually the product is CH2= C(Ar1)Ar2. The reverse would be O= C(Ar1)Ar2 (a carbonyl attached to two aromatic rings) plus LiCH2Si(C)(C)C. But the carbonyl is likely a benzaldehyde derivative? Wait the carbonyl is attached to two aromatic rings? The forward reaction: O=[C:2]([c:3]... ) [c:11]... . So carbonyl carbon attached to two aromatic groups (aryl-aryl ketone). That's a diaryl ketone (benzophenone). The product is CH2= C(Ar1)Ar2 (alkene). So the retrosynthesis: target alkene -> diaryl ketone + LiCH2Si(C)(C)C.

Thus we need to apply template to target molecule to get precursors list. Use apply_template tool with molecule_smiles = target SMILES and template_id = 1679747.

Let's call apply_template.
